subtitle: Filtering and transforming records in a single readable line.

eyebrow: The four-line version, with a loop
caption: Four lines to express one simple idea: the order IDs where status is Shipped.

eyebrow: The same idea, as a one-line list comprehension
code:
shipped_ids = [row["order_id"] for row in orders if row["status"] == "Shipped"]
print(shipped_ids)   # [1001, 1005]

# No filter -- just transforming every item:
line_totals = [row["quantity"] * row["unit_price"] for row in orders]
caption: Read it left to right: row['order_id'] -- for each row in orders -- if status is Shipped. Same three ingredients, one line.

eyebrow: Dict comprehensions -- building instant lookups by key
caption: order_totals_by_id[1001] is instant -- no scanning the whole list for the row where order_id equals 1001.

eyebrow: A dict comprehension with a filter
caption: Same filter condition as a list comprehension's -- just building a dict instead of a list.
